emma: Heads-up: saw a ~18% p95 latency regression on Llama-3-13B chat infra after the recent rope_theta default change. Mostly on multi-turn sessions with long system prompts.
raj: Oof. Is that across hosted + dedicated or just one pool?
emma: Seen on both, but dedicated less noisy. Host trace attached from a dev cluster run.
perf-bot: trace uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/2083056789/llama3-13b-chat-prefetch-2026-03-18
emma: Quick profiler dump (top hotspots):
```
hotspots:
  matmul_generic_kernel         39.8%  # unexpected
  kv_cache_copy                 21.4%
  kernel_selector_fallback      12.7%
  attention_kv_prefetch         8.9%
  memcpy                        6.1%
```
emma: previous runs used matmul_tuned_128 which was ~35% faster for our head dim distribution.

sasha: Kernel selector is falling back because of head_dim alignment mismatch after rope_theta change? That seems odd but plausible if sequence length distribution changed and we hit a path with different kernel heuristics.

marta: I dug into the traces — for many requests we now see head_dim=128 with sequence len spikes >1024 due to chat templates. The selector chooses a conservative matmul path tuned for large sequences which isn't well-optimized for our 13B head layout.

raj: Could this be KV cache thrash too? If attention prefetch window is larger, we do more kv_cache_copy per token.

sasha: Yep. The prefetch heuristics kick in when rope_theta -> default changed behavior for extrapolated positions. That expands effective sequence range used in the selector logic, causing different kernel choices + extra KV movement.

marta: Repro command to force the variant locally:
```
RUN_INFERENCE --model llm-llama3-13b \
  --runtime.override_kernel_selector="prefer:matmul_tuned_128" \
  --runtime.kv_prefetch_window=32
```
marta: With that override p95 dropped ~14% in a canary run.

emma: Nice. Short-term mitigation: pin kernel selector for the 13B flavor and reduce kv_prefetch_window in chat-heavy routes.

raj: Longer term: we should update the selector heuristics to consider (head_dim, hidden_size) pair explicitly alongside sequence length and rope theta. Currently sequence length dominates decision.

sasha: Agreed. Also add a fast-path for head_dim % 32 == 0 and sequence_len in [64,1024] to pick matmul_tuned_128.

marta: One more wrinkle: RMSNorm->SiLU configuration changes in model variant we onboarded last week changed intermediate MLP memory pattern, slightly increasing memcpy pressure during matmul, which amplifies the kernel choice impact.

emma: So root causes: rope_theta default tweak changed effective position scaling -> different seq len behavior -> selector picks slower kernel + kv prefetch increases -> memcpy/kv_copy costs climb -> RMSNorm/SiLU memory pattern makes it worse.

raj: Action items:
- emma: create a canary patch that forces kernel selector override on a subset of hosts (deadline: today EOD)
- marta: add a unit test in kernel-selector that enumerates head_dim x seq_len combos and asserts the chosen kernel is expected (PR by tomorrow)
- sasha: propose selector heuristic change to consider head_dim alignment (RFC in #eng-runtime, cc @emma)
- infra: reduce kv_prefetch_window on chat routes from 64 -> 32 as a temporary knob

marta: Proposed selector snippet for override (runtime flag):
```
--runtime.selector.policy_override="if model==llama3 && head_dim==128 && seq_len<=1024 then select matmul_tuned_128"
```

sasha: Smart. Also add telemetry so we can correlate head_dim/seq_len bucket -> kernel choice -> latency.

perf-bot: canary test queued on dedicated-canary-3, will post results when done.

deploy-bot: rolling the override to 10% hosts now, will stop if errors > 1% or p95 doesn't improve in 15m.

emma: Thanks — I'll watch the canary, and post the before/after perf numbers here. If canary looks good, schedule a controlled rollout + add selector unit tests and telemetry.

raj: One more thought — chat templates: consider truncating system prompt embedding or enabling prefix-cache to avoid sequence length spikes. That buys us more margin before touching selector heuristics.

emma: noted. I'll coordinate with product to trial shorter system prompts for the affected routes.

sasha: +1. Also add a perf regression alert that specifically watches kernel_selector_fallback% in the trace metrics. It would've caught this earlier.

emma: OK team — tracking in the thread. (reaction :thumbsup:)
